features.name: Large fief building system with two build queues and a management screen
features.summary: Every town, castle and village can hold about 33 building types (mills, mines, quarries, fisheries, guard posts, watchtowers, messenger posts, prison tower, training ground, slave market, sewers, baths, a temple of the holder's faith, and very expensive prestige monuments up to 300,000 silver). Names and descriptions change with the settlement's culture. Two buildings can be under construction at once; finished buildings give prosperity, renown, relation and troop experience over time. The holder manages it all from a graphical management screen that also offers garrison exchange and a brutal 'repopulate' option.
features.mechanics: Building ids are party slots 128-160 (value >=1 = built). get_improvement_details (1009 stmts, Native 32) maps id -> culture-specific name/description in s0/s1 and cost in reg0 (e.g. 141 guard posts 15000, 133 iron mine 80000, 156 150000, 160 300000; 142 = temple whose name follows the holder's religion, 8000). improve_center(center, builder, days) puts $g_improvement_type into the first free queue (slot 162 with finish-hour 163, else 164/165) and records the builder in 272/273; gives the builder +3 renown or the player 200 xp. strig:74 (every ~1.6 min game time) walks one centre per tick ($g_set_center_upgrades) and calls cf_check_building_finished for both queues: when the finish hour passes it sets the building slot, messages the holder and applies one-off effects (prosperity, honour, piety, relation, walker types). strig:141 (every 2.1h, random town/castle) applies recurring effects: 157/158/160 add prosperity and +5 owner renown and +1/+2 player relation, 149 (training ground) upgrades the garrison with 30-50k xp, 159 adds renown. The UI is prsnt_center_management started by mst:center_management (t0 every frame), reached from menu:center_manage_2 (town 'Manage this town/fortress', village 'Manage this village'); its event handler (prsnt:center_management/t2) sets $g_improvement_type and links to menu_garrison_management (swap troops with the garrison) and menu_repopulate (needs >=200 men and negative relation). Fire disasters (see ad457.settlement_disasters_epidemics) can destroy buildings.

features.name: AI lords spend their wealth: build in fiefs, hire mercenaries, upgrade their own gear
features.summary: When a lord visits his own town or castle he collects its accumulated rents and tariffs, and if he is rich (over 10,000) he commissions a building there himself. In towns and castles he can also hire the local mercenary stack for cash, and he trades his weapons/armour for better-quality versions (better item modifiers) at the town armourer, capped by an equipment budget that depends on his personality and his kingdom's policy.
features.mechanics: troop_does_business_in_center (323 stmts; Native 52) runs whenever a lord is in a centre. Owner visit: adds party slots 47+48 (accumulated rents/tariffs) to troop wealth slot 11 and zeroes them. If $g_dplmc_ai_changes>=1, wealth >10000 and a build queue (162 or 164) is free: picks a random building id (128-145 for villages, 140-156 for towns/castles), filters by preconditions (e.g. 146/134 need the lord's culture != centre culture, 128 silver mine needs party 241, 133/138 need party 239), prices it with get_improvement_details scaled by faction slot 303 and the lord's Engineer skill (and prisoners as labour), deducts gold and calls improve_center. Villages: adds the village's queued recruits (party 88/89) to his party. Towns/castles: may hire mercenaries from party slots 90/91 using game_get_join_cost, budget = wealth/(faction slot 304 + 10). Then calculate_equipment_limit (3000, halved for reputation types 1-2, -1000 for type 8, -100 x faction slot 302) caps spending while it swaps each equipped item for a better-modifier copy in the town's armourer/weaponsmith/horse-merchant (party 21/22/24) paying the value difference, and finally fixes troop class (horse -> cavalry, ranged weapon -> archer).

features.name: Seasonal disasters and epidemics in settlements
features.summary: Towns and villages can be hit by epidemics, droughts, crop failures, fires and (rarely) earthquakes. Odds depend on the season and on buildings: sewers/baths and similar make plague less likely, while fires burn down several of the settlement's buildings. A hit costs prosperity and cuts the settlement's stored rents; the fief owner gets a notification menu describing what happened, and the event stays on the settlement (it shows in its management screen, rumours and ideal prosperity) until it expires.
features.mechanics: Five random-centre triggers set an event code in party slot 800 (disaster) or 801 (epidemic) when that slot is 0: strig:142 (every 0.74h, towns/castles) epidemic: chance = season factor (1-3 by $g_cur_month) out of (180 - prosperity + 25, +100 if building 152, +50 if 145), severity 5-35 (-1 if both buildings), sets 801, notifies via menu_epidemic_outbreak; strig:143 (villages, code 120, odds out of 250-300, +200 with building 139, -50 with 135); strig:144 (villages, code 130, odds out of 350-400); strig:145 (all centres, code 100, 1/700, rents x0.25 - the earthquake-class event); strig:146 (towns, code 110 fire: 300 base, season 20-50, building 148 halves risk, port towns +25; loops building slots 128-156 except a protected list and randomly clears up to N buildings, owner gets 'The fire in {s60} de...' per building). Each sets party 47 (accumulated rents) to 75% (25% for code 100) and applies prosperity change reg1 from get_event_details (109 stmts: code -> name/description/prosperity effect). strig:47 (every 0.37h) reads/clears slot 800 over time; get_center_ideal_prosperity, center_get_capital, get_rumor_to_s61 and prsnt:center_management read it.

features.name: Faiths for lords and kingdoms, player conversion, piety and battle blessings
features.summary: Every kingdom has an official faith (five Christian confessions, Roman paganism, Germanic/steppe paganism, two Zoroastrian schools, Judaism) and every lord has a personal faith. Every three days a random lord may convert to his kingdom's (or culture's) faith, which is announced. The player picks a faith at the start, can convert by talking to bishops/abbots/high priests, can dedicate himself to a pagan pantheon at shrines (which raises relation with lords of that faith), and earns piety by praying, sacrificing, donating, funding memorials and through event choices. With piety above 25 the player may receive a random blessing in battle (allies faster, damage changes, or the player healed). Religious sites are real map locations with monasteries, temples and shrines.
features.mechanics: Faith codes 0-9 (0 Chalcedonian, 1 Arian, 2 Miaphysite, 3 Nestorian, 4 Donatist, 5 Paganism, 6 Roman paganism, 7 Mazdaist, 8 Zurvanite, 9 Judaism). init_religions (from game_start, 160 stmts) assigns religion factions (fac_roman_christians, fac_arian_christians, fac_coptic_christians, fac_nestorian_christians, fac_donatist_christians, fac_pagans, fac_roman_pagans, fac_zoroastrians...) to p_religious_site_* parties with scenes (christian_monastery, fire_temple, german_temple_*, celtic_stone_circle, steppe_shrine, roman_pagan_temple, siwa) and abbot/priest troops. Kingdom faith = faction slot 13, lord faith = troop slot 15 (spouse slot 30 follows). strig:15 (every 72h) calls check_lord_religion on a random hero: if his faith differs from his kingdom's, he converts when the kingdom is one of a listed set or his culture (troop 44) matches, and a log line names the new faith. Player faith $g_player_faith set by menu_religion_selection, MCC presets, player_is_king/lord, and conversion dialogs (dlg:4686, 4700, 4712, 4724, 5932-5981); the player can also ask a lord to convert (dlg:1204 lord_talk_convert, dlg:1208-1225 choices, each setting the lord's troop 15). $piety written by menu:religious_location_christian/generic options (pray/sacrifice +1 piety and 1 hour, memorial +5 honour, donate 500, raid, seize the monastery), event menus and quest dialogs. menu:religious_location_generic dedication options call change_player_relation_lords_religion(faith, amount), which loops lords and changes relation by faith match. mst:lead_charge/t91 (and the same trigger in other battle templates; check 3s, rearm 100000000 = once per battle) with $piety>25 and 16% chance applies a random blessing: allied agent_set_damage_modifier 95 or 110, agent_set_speed_modifier 110, or heals the player to full. Temple building 142 (ad457.center_buildings_management) is named after the holder's faith.

features.name: Town revolts that spawn rebel kingdoms, plus rebel reconciliation and riots in ownerless towns
features.summary: Towns can rise in revolt: a rebel army appears and besieges the town, and if it wins, the town becomes the seat of a new breakaway kingdom named after it, using the culture and troops of the kingdom it left. Later, a sufficiently old rebel kingdom of the right culture may make peace with and rejoin the Western Roman Empire, handing back its towns and lords while its leader becomes an outlaw. Towns that end up with no proper owner are besieged by rioting citizens.

Separately, with 1/50 chance for specific towns of listed kingdoms, cf_start_rebellion(town, parent faction) takes a free pooled faction from fac_rebel_kingdom_1..3 (faction slot 21 == 2 = unused), renames it after the town, copies culture (10), banner/troop slots 15/22/40-59 and reinforcement templates 77-79 from the parent (Hispania templates for listed towns), sets 811=3 (countdown) and 812 cooldown. strig:15 (72h) reconciliation: a rebel faction at peace with fac_kingdom_1, same culture, faction slot 1450 > 30, 1/20 chance -> marked defeated (21=2), its lords join kingdom_1, its centres go to kingdom_1, its leader becomes an outlaw, its parties change faction, player shown menu_rebels_join_rome. strig:117 (72h): any town/castle owned by fac_manhunters or fac_commoners gets a 600-man 'Rioting Citizens' party (fac_outlaws, besieging, ignore player).

features.name: Weak kingdoms become tributaries; provocations lead to reparation demands
features.summary: Kingdoms reduced to one to three fortresses look for protection: every two days one such kingdom may submit as a tributary to a stronger enemy that has a grudge against it, paying 20,000 and making peace; its other wars are ended or joined to its overlord's. The player's kingdom can be offered a tributary in the same way. When one realm has a casus belli against another, the aggrieved ruler may demand reparations (8,000 per town, 4,000 per castle of the offender) instead of going straight to war; the offender pays or war starts. The player can be on either side of such a demand.
features.mechanics: strig:127 (every 48h): random active kingdom with faction slots 81+82 (castles+towns) in 1-3; for every active faction, reads the computed per-pair faction arrays at 820+other (friendly treaty state, >40 counted) and 1020+other (grievance/provocation score); picks the hostile faction with the highest grievance that is bigger, compares against a resistance score 300 - 30*(#factions it has grievances over) + 30*holdings + 30*friends; if beaten calls dplmc_start_tributary_between_kingdoms(weak, strong, 1), or if the strong one is the player's kingdom raises menu_notification_tributary_offer. dplmc_start_tributary_between_kingdoms (97 stmts): faction slot 100 = overlord, relation +15 (min 40), prisoner exchange, rulers' wealth -/+20000, player relation updates, notification menu_dplmc_notification_tribute_declared, peace both ways, sets 820+ pair slots to 160 and clears 1020+ grievances, makes the tributary leave wars with overlord's friends and join the overlord's wars. strig:27 -> randomly_start_war_peace_new_for_faction (269 stmts, per-faction variant of Native's war/peace script) raises menu_notification_casus_belli_decide: both sides run npc_decision_checklist_peace_or_war, ruler reputation types 1/4/5 are more aggressive; result is war, menu_notification_tribute_demanded (if the player rules the offender), reparations paid via add_to_troop_wealth, or war on refusal. menu_decide_ai_tribute handles the player's own demand. Expiries via menu_dplmc_notification_tribute_expired_*.

features.name: Garrison reinforcements march in from the fief's villages
features.summary: Instead of soldiers appearing out of thin air in a castle or town, the holder's money buys reinforcements that are raised in the centre's bound villages and walk to the fortress as visible map parties ('X reinforcements'). They can be intercepted. The amount depends on the centre's treasury, difficulty setting and kingdom policy; the troop mix comes from the kingdom's (or the player's chosen culture's) three reinforcement templates.
features.mechanics: strig:23 (every ~9 min, rotating $center_to_check over towns/castles) calls prune_prisoners then hire_men_to_center(center). hire_men_to_center (130 stmts): only for lord-owned centres not under siege (party 54 == -1); cost per batch 300/450/600 by game_get_reduce_campaign_ai (player's own kingdom fixed 450, 1 batch); uses faction slots 77/78/79 (Native reinforcement templates; player culture when $g_king_start and $g_player_culture set; special cases for fac_indigenoi castles). features.name: Kings without a town take one; lords of fortress-less kingdoms defect or disband
features.summary: Every frame one kingdom is checked. If its king owns no town but the kingdom has a town with no lord, the king is given it. If the kingdom has lost every town and castle, its lords look for a new kingdom and defect (announced in the log); those who cannot leave have their war parties disbanded when idle, and the rest lose 50 relation with their king.

features.name: Court offices for vassals and a title ladder for the player
features.summary: Kingdoms hand out named offices (e.g. Magister Militum per Gallia, Magister Officiorum, Comes Africae, Eran-Spahbed) to their most respected lords, and a ruling player can appoint vassals to offices through the minister. A player serving Rome rises through honorary ranks - Vir Clarissimus, then Spectabilis, then Illustris - as his relation with the emperor reaches 15, 30 and 50, each announced by a promotion screen. Titles show in lord names and notes.
features.mechanics: assign_rank(office, faction): among the faction's lords without an office (troop 155 == 0) and with rank >= 1 (troop 156), pick the one with the best relation-to-ruler + renown/2 (min 300), set troop 155 = office, then troop_set_title_according_to_faction (modified, 165 stmts) rebuilds his displayed name; called from change_troop_faction and indict_lord_for_treason so offices are refilled when holders leave. features.name: Independent tribes with capitals, patrols, migration, conquest and tribute
features.summary: About 37 small independent peoples (Aestii, Dani, Frisians, Vascones, Garamantes, steppe hordes and others) each have a capital, a king, a garrison and roaming patrols. The player can visit, recruit their warriors, attack the capital, and afterwards loot it, pillage it or turn the tribe into a tributary that pays a monthly tribute; tributary kings can be asked for levies or a special tribute. Nomadic tribes periodically pack up their camp, travel across the map and settle somewhere new.

features.name: Start the game as ruler or vassal of an existing kingdom
features.summary: At game start the player can choose 'Royal Sandbox' to take over an existing kingdom as its ruler (picking from a kingdom-selection screen), or start as a landed lord, instead of the usual nobody start. The chosen realm's former ruler steps aside, the player gets its fortresses, faith and culture, and the realm keeps its existing alliances and tributaries. Character creation itself uses a one-screen point-buy menu.

features.name: Diplomacy 4.x extras: tax inefficiency, disguises, taverngoer locations
features.summary: Holding more fiefs than your administration can handle costs money: past a difficulty-based number of fiefs, each extra fief loses a growing share (up to 65%) of its taxes, reduced by having a chamberlain, a court and a spouse, and shifted by the kingdom's centralisation/policy settings. features.name: Targeted per-kingdom AI recalculation instead of world-wide rethinks
features.summary: When something changes for a kingdom (war or peace, a treaty, a centre changing hands, a lord changing sides, a battle result, a marshal change), 457 AD re-plans only the kingdoms involved, immediately, instead of setting Native's 'recalculate everything' flag that makes every kingdom and every lord re-plan. A slow round-robin also refreshes one kingdom per tick. This keeps campaign AI responsive and cheaper on big maps.
features.mechanics: recalculate_ais_for_faction(faction) (13 stmts): for kingdoms (fac_player_supporters_faction..fac_manhunters) and minor factions -> init_ai_calculation_new(faction) (re-computes party strengths and nearby friend/enemy strengths only for that faction's lord parties, its centres and the player) -> decide_faction_ai(faction) -> calculate_troop_ai for that faction's lords only. 39 call sites replace Native's $g_recalculate_ais flag: diplomacy_start_war/peace_between_kingdoms and every dplmc_start_*_between_kingdoms (both factions), give_center_to_faction, change_troop_faction, player_join/leave_faction, activate_player_faction, game_event_simulate_battle, event_player_captured_as_prisoner, process_hero_ai, cf_launch_rebellion, marshal/feast/call-to-arms dialogs. strig:41 also calls it for one faction per tick. The global recalculate_ais remains only on the debug 'Force rethink for all factions' option.
